thread:
maria: Heads-up — DeltaHead sales signed LOI for 1.2M GPU hours/year. They want reserved pools in eu-west-1 and us-west-2, +20% burst buffer. Need us to confirm buffer policy & cost implications before contract.

ajay: Congrats. Do they need guaranteed p99 latency? Any concurrency / sequence length profile?

maria: They've given typical seq len 512, median token rate ~1.5k tok/s per request, peak concurrent streams ~200. They're sensitive to latency spikes; prefer <120ms generation p50. Also want canary rollout and region failover.

linh: Proposal thought: Offer 10% reserved + 15% burst credits billed as on-demand at a discounted multiplier, with rollover. Or alternatively commit floor 1.0M + a 200k burst bucket. Which is simpler for contract?

tom: From infra — eu-west capacity is tight next quarter (A100 pool constrained). To guarantee 1.2M +20% we'd need to either carve dedicated nodes early or allow cross-region spill. Cross-region adds ~12-18ms RTT which may break their latency target.

maria: Important: DeltaHead requires EU data residency for eu-west traffic, so cross-region routing for EU workloads is not acceptable.

tom: Ok, then eu-west must be provisioned in-region. Quick back-of-envelope: 1 A100-equivalent sustained ~= 8M tokens/hr for our gen profile. If we split 60/40 eu/us, eu needs ~720k GPU-hours => sustained ~82 GPUs year-round. Add 10-20% headroom => ~90-100 GPUs dedicated. That's non-trivial capacity.

ajay: Can we use mixed instance types (a few cheaper GA10x / RTX45xx) for non-latency-critical paths to lower cost?

tom: Mixed types are feasible if model variants/quantization are validated. Ops complexity and orchestration (~sharding, kernel differences) go up though. Also note network egress/peering costs are already accounted for in the dedicated offering.

linh: From solutions perspective: recommend two-tier commit: regional guaranteed baseline + optional global burst pool billed by usage (prepaid credits or pay-as-you-go). SLA-backed latency only on the baseline. Burst gets best-effort with a clear pricing multiplier.

maria: Customer is pushing for a firm buffer so their launches (Q3 marketing push) don't get throttled. They also want an explicit rollback & credit formula if we fail to deliver burst capacity during declared launch windows.

tom: Suggest policy draft: baseline commit = 1.0M GPU-hrs (regionally split in contract). Burst bucket = 200k GPU-hrs at 1.6x on-demand price. If we cannot provide burst during agreed windows, issue service credits equal to 2x the burst value for the unavailable hours. Example formula:
```
if burst_unavailable_hours > 0:
  credit = burst_unavailable_hours * burst_rate * 2
```

ajay: Pricing sanity check: our blended on-demand cost ~ $3.2 / GPU-hr, dedicated marginal ops cost ~ $1.8 / GPU-hr. To hit revenue targets while giving a discount on baseline, burst at $4.8 / GPU-hr is reasonable (1.5x on-demand). Need to run margin vs churn simulation.

linh: Also include an auto-bump clause for seasonal spikes: if sustained usage >90% of baseline for 7 days, trigger capacity review + optional temporary commit top-up (customer can accept or we offer temporary degraded throughput).

maria: I'll draft a commercial appendix listing regional baselines, burst pricing, credits formula, and an ops playbook (canary steps, runbook, escalation path).

ops-bot: Note: scheduled maintenance windows may affect burst availability; ensure maintenance blackout windows and notice periods are included in SLA appendix.

tom: Action items: I'll run a usage simulator with DeltaHead's profile (seq len distribution, concurrency, diurnal patterns) and produce required A100-equivalent node counts, node types, and cost delta. ETA: EOD tomorrow.

ajay: I'll prep the commercial appendix and loop in legal for the credit wording. @maria can you own the customer call to review the appendix?

maria: Yep — I'll set a call for Thursday 09:30 PT and invite solutions + infra. Thanks everyone.
